answer: Bind standing to a banded falcon flown across a meadow transect. Each flight ends with the holder filing the bird's radar echo signature, which unlocks the next flight permit, so flights run in order and one bird serves no second holder. A copied echo fails: wingbeat cadence and turn pattern differ per bird, and replays mismatch transect radar. Banding and training one falcon costs $540 plus 38 handler hours. Ten thousand identities would demand ten thousand falcons, $5,400,000, and 380,000 handler hours, and no bulk purchase breeds a second bird with the same echo.
